lines.text: Triangle angles show up on every single SAT. Here is the one shortcut that saves you half the work.
Start with any triangle: three interior angles, A, B, and C.
Slide A and B up next to C, and they snap into a flat straight line: A plus B plus C always equals one eighty.
Now extend the bottom side past C. That outside corner is the exterior angle, d.
Notice that C plus d is also a straight line, one eighty! Drop C from both, and boom: the exterior angle d equals A plus B.
So if A is fifty-two degrees and B is seventy-one, don't touch C! Just add fifty-two plus seventy-one: one twenty-three.
On a harder SAT problem, they hide it in algebra: A is two x plus twelve, B is x plus nineteen, and the exterior angle is one twenty-one.
Set A plus B equal to the outside angle: three x plus thirty-one equals one twenty-one. Three x is ninety, so x equals thirty!
